prose.notes: head_index = None means whole-fixture membership and is stored as the sentinel groups_db::WHOLE_FIXTURE, not NULL — a port must keep that sentinel, since remove_fixture_from_group's split logic depends on it. Adding a head to a fixture that already has whole-fixture membership is subsumed server-side, so the store only does an optimistic update for whole-fixture adds and refetches the hierarchy for head adds (and refetches on error too).
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Group(group_id) ONLY — the fixture is not separately authorized
Inserts a membership row; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()

prose.callerUsage: appendThreadMessages() diffs current messages against the persisted baseline (persisted must be an exact prefix), sends only the tail, sets expectedHeadMessageId = last baseline id ?? null, and reuses ONE in-flight operationId per thread (pendingTranscriptAppends) so a lost IPC response can be retried for the exact committed result. It then verifies returned rows are same-thread, id/role-matched, and contiguous with the previous seq.
prose.notes: COMPARE-AND-SWAP: the Rust command COLLAPSES the typed AgentThreadAppendOutcome::HeadMoved variant into a plain Err string ("Agent transcript changed before append (expected X, found Y); reload the conversation before retrying"). SMELL: a structured, expected outcome is only distinguishable by parsing an error message over IPC — a port should consider surfacing the variant. `expectedHeadMessageId: null` explicitly asserts an empty transcript (not 'don't care'). Per-message `id` is optional (server generates a uuid) but the frontend always supplies the UIMessage id; `seq` is never caller-supplied. Never rebases implicitly — the caller must reload or fork.
prose.returns: AgentThreadMessage[] — only the newly appended rows, in order, with DB-assigned contiguous seq
sideEffects: one SQLite transaction commits the message batch and its idempotent response record together
bumps the thread's updatedAt / transcript head

prose.callerUsage: createThread(input) wraps it as `{ input }`; createScopedThread builds requestId=crypto.randomUUID(), never sends the principal, retries once with the SAME payload on failure (relying on requestId idempotency), then fail-closed validates the returned row with threadMatchesScope().
prose.notes: Owner is derived from auth::admitted_principal(db) — the caller CANNOT set ownerUserId; `null` owner is the signed-out principal, a real value, not 'unknown'. agentKind/subjectKind are plain strings on the wire but the backend enforces a closed routing invariant (models/agent_threads.rs authored_route): track_copilot requires subjectKind="track" + non-empty subjectId/venueId/scoreId and NO implementationId; pattern_graph requires subjectKind="pattern" + non-empty subjectId/implementationId and NO scoreId. Anything else errors.
prose.returns: AgentThread { id, ownerUserId, agentKind, subjectKind, subjectId, implementationId, venueId, scoreId, forkedFromThreadId, forkedAtMessageId, parentThreadId, parentCallId, title, actor, createdAt, updatedAt }
sideEffects: inserts the thread row (SQLite) AND initializes/attaches its authored document in the same operation
idempotent on requestId — a retried identical payload returns the previously created thread instead of a duplicate

when parentThreadId is set (a subagent), also allocates the child's authored workspace from the parent's current head, keyed by the same requestId; the child's turns then prepare and finalize against that private head instead of the live document

prose.callerUsage: deleteThread() awaits the invoke then clears the thread's entry from the pendingTranscriptAppends idempotency map.
prose.notes: Authored REVISION HISTORY survives deletion and remains restorable — this is not a cascade purge of authored state (consistent with the project's no-cascade-deletes rule). The retire-before-delete ordering is load-bearing: it closes admission so an in-flight host call can't write after the branch disappears. Needs four backend services wired (Db, AuthoredDocuments, PythonWorkspaceService, GraphRunStore).
sideEffects: ORDERED teardown: for each child authored workspace, PythonWorkspaceService::retire_thread(workspaceId) then GraphRunStore::forget(workspaceId); then retire_thread(threadId) and forget(threadId); only then is the thread row deleted
kills/drains sandboxed Python kernels and drops published graph runs
deletes the thread row and its authored workspaces

prose.callerUsage: loadThreadMessages() maps rows to AI-SDK UIMessages, substituting `[{type:'text',text:''}]` for an empty parts array, validates every message with isAgentChatMessage and throws (fail-closed, no partial history) if any row fails; builds the append baseline with partsJson computed from the CLIENT message, not the echoed row.
prose.notes: Messages come back ordered by `seq` ascending; `seq` is i64 exported as TS number and is DB-assigned. `parts` is the AI SDK UIMessage.parts array verbatim — opaque JSON the backend never interprets; it round-trips through serde_json and MAY have object keys reordered, so never byte-compare the echoed parts. A thread owned by another principal is not visible (scoped by ownerUserId).
sideEffects: read-only SQLite query scoped to the admitted principal

prose.callerUsage: listThreads() explicitly sends `?? null` for each filter (never omits them); listScopedThreads() then re-filters client-side on the full ExactThreadScope (principal, implementationId, venueId, scoreId) because the command has no filter for those fields.
prose.notes: Each filter is an independent AND; null = wildcard for that field. Backend orders newest-first but the frontend deliberately re-picks with newestThread() (updatedAt desc, createdAt tiebreak) so behavior doesn't depend on SQL ordering — a port should not rely on the server order. No pagination. Three of the seven identity fields are NOT filterable server-side; that filtering must happen in the client.
sideEffects: read-only SQLite query scoped to the admitted principal

prose.callerUsage: renameThread(threadId, title) passes the title through unchanged; `null` is a real value meaning 'clear the title'.
prose.notes: Title is display metadata and is deliberately NOT part of ExactThreadScope / thread identity. No idempotency key — last write wins.
sideEffects: updates title (and updatedAt) on the thread row, scoped to the admitted principal

prose.notes: Schema-free by design — the frontend builds { event, route, data } where data carries a jsHeap snapshot (performance.memory, null on non-Chromium). Because it's a blocking sync command it runs on the IPC thread and does real disk IO per call; callers are expected to be low-frequency. Errors are swallowed by the TS side (console.error only). Only one rotation generation is kept.
sideEffects: mkdir -p app_config_dir
rotates $APPCONFIG/render-telemetry.log → render-telemetry.log.1 when it exceeds 5 MiB (removing any prior .1)
appends one JSON line: { ts: RFC3339 UTC, entry: <payload> }

prose.callerUsage: checkAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; snapshotId feeds straight into commit's `expectedSnapshotId`.
prose.notes: NOT a pure read — it repairs the workspace on disk. `snapshotId` is a hash of the exact raw files inspected and is the compare-and-swap token for commit_workspace, so check→commit must be adjacent with no intervening writes. `changed` means raw files diverge from the detached head; for track workspaces changed is effectively always false because raw divergence is repaired rather than reported (track children author only through structured Python ops). `document` is the CANDIDATE projection decoded from raw files, which may not equal any stored revision.
prose.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceCheck { id, headRevisionId, snapshotId, changed, document }
sideEffects: reads the raw workspace directory; RESTORES any missing required files from the head revision
for TRACK-scope documents only, if raw files differ from head files it OVERWRITES the workspace directory with the head files (repairing a stale post-commit materialization) and reports changed=false

prose.callerUsage: commitAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; expectedHeadRevisionId comes from the handle/check and expectedSnapshotId from check_workspace.
prose.notes: DOUBLE compare-and-swap: both expectedHeadRevisionId AND expectedSnapshotId must still hold. `operationId` is a validated idempotency token; `message` is normalized to a subject line (normalized_subject) and is required. Note the field is `appliedToCurrentWorkspace` here, whereas turn/restore/merge results use `appliedToCurrentProjection` — the semantics differ (workspace detached head vs document head) and a port must not unify them. Commit does NOT touch the document head; merge_workspace does.
prose.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceCommit { id, revisionId, appliedToCurrentWorkspace, changed, document }
sideEffects: creates a new revision on the workspace's DETACHED branch (not the document head) and advances the workspace head
enqueues sync closure

prose.callerUsage: createAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; only id/baseRevisionId/headRevisionId reach the frontend.
prose.notes: The absolute workspace PATH is deliberately never serialized across IPC — AuthoredWorkspace (internal) has `path`, AuthoredWorkspaceHandle (IPC) does not, and there is a unit test (authored_state.rs:262) asserting the path never leaks. A port must keep that boundary. `requestId` is the idempotency key, validated as a token; reusing it against a different base/document errors ('workspace request id is already bound to another base or document'), and a retired request errors too. headRevisionId == baseRevisionId at creation. Workspace file limits: max 8 files, 16 MiB per file, 64 MiB total.
sideEffects: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(owner_thread_id, request_id) DO NOTHING into authored_subagent_workspaces (idempotent reservation)
materializes the revision's files into a bounded plain directory on disk (the workspace path)

prose.callerUsage: finalizeAuthoredTurn(input) with `{ input }`; callers must branch on `status`.
prose.notes: A conflict is a NORMAL return value, not an error — do not treat non-committed as failure. On 'committed', `revisionId` is this operation's revision even if the head has since advanced; `appliedToCurrentProjection` tells you whether it is still the head, while `document` is ALWAYS the current projection and safe to hydrate. `changed` distinguishes a no-op commit. Conflicts carry a structured path (AuthoredMergePathSegment discriminated on `kind`/`value`) with base/ours/theirs as {state:'missing'} | {state:'present', value:unknown}; score_layer values are TS `number`, deliberately not bigint.
prose.returns: AuthoredTurnCommit — tagged by `status`: { status:'committed', documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection, changed, document } | { status:'conflicted', documentId, preparedRevisionId, conflicts: AuthoredMergeConflict[] }
sideEffects: commits the prepared revision into the document lineage (may 3-way merge against a head that advanced)
enqueues sync closure; retires/consumes the turn preparation row

prose.callerUsage: listAuthoredHistory(threadId, cursor = null, limit = 100) — the 100 default lives in TS, not in Rust.
prose.notes: Cursor is OPAQUE and stable over the union of current-lineage revisions and superseded proposal tips — never construct or parse it. Entry fields: revisionId, parentIds[] (merge revisions have >1), message, authoredAt (RFC 3339), threadId?, assistantMessageId?, kind (AuthoredOperationKind, snake_case: initial_import|edit|agent_turn|restore|pattern_fork|workspace_merge|sync_integration|revision — `revision` is the forward-compat catch-all for newer producers, so a port must NOT exhaustively reject unknown kinds), position (current|ancestor|superseded — superseded tips are still restorable), proposalSequence (i64 exported as `number | null`; server-assigned cross-device ordering), and conversationCheckpoint {threadId, assistantMessageId} present ONLY when the revision sits exactly on an immutable assistant-turn boundary — i.e. it gates whether state_and_conversation restore is offerable. `limit` being null means the backend default applies.
sideEffects: read-only

prose.callerUsage: mergeAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; callers branch on `status`.
prose.notes: Conflicted is a normal outcome, not an error. Note the ASYMMETRY with AuthoredTurnCommit::Conflicted: this variant carries ONLY `conflicts` — no documentId, no preparedRevisionId — so a shared conflict-rendering component cannot assume those fields. `expectedHeadRevisionId` is the workspace head CAS (the document head may have advanced; that's what the merge resolves). The workspace is not automatically removed after a successful merge — see authored_state_remove_workspace.
prose.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceMerge — tagged by `status`: { status:'merged', documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection, document } | { status:'conflicted', conflicts: AuthoredMergeConflict[] }
sideEffects: 3-way merges the workspace's detached head into the parent document and writes a merge revision (parentIds has 2 entries in history)
enqueues sync closure; on conflict nothing is written

prose.callerUsage: prepareAuthoredTurn(input) invokes with `{ input }` and the returned preparedRevisionId is carried into finalize.
prose.notes: IDEMPOTENT on (threadId, assistantMessageId): a repeat returns the existing preparation, but if `graph` is supplied and its file encoding differs from the recorded snapshot it errors with 'assistant message id was already prepared with another graph'. `graph` is pattern-only: supplying it on a track thread errors ('track assistant turns cannot prepare a graph'); omitting it snapshots the current head files. `document` is the tagged union AuthoredProjectedDocument: {kind:'track_score', revision} | {kind:'pattern_graph', implementationId, revision, graph} — snake_case tag values, camelCase fields. Invariant (per project memory): one prepared authored turn per assistant row.
sideEffects: takes the thread's authored write lock, inserts a new revision parented on the current head
INSERTs into authored_turn_preparations (thread_id, assistant_message_id, …) — one prepared turn per assistant message
enqueues the revision closure for sync and, when signed in, enqueues a local sync row for authored_turn_preparations

prose.callerUsage: recoverAuthoredTurns(threadId) — flat `{ threadId }` payload (NOT wrapped in `input`, unlike its prepare/finalize siblings).
prose.notes: Crash-recovery sweep; safe to call on load. Argument-shape inconsistency with prepare/finalize is a real ergonomics smell for a port: some authored_state commands take `{ input: {...} }`, others take flat scalars. Ordering of the returned array follows preparation order; each element must be branched on `status` exactly like finalize.
prose.returns: AuthoredTurnCommit[] (same tagged union as finalize, one per recovered preparation)
sideEffects: finalizes any prepared-but-unfinalized turns left behind by a crash/restart; writes revisions and sync closures for each

prose.notes: ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING and must be preserved by any port: authorize -> retire python execution (drain in-flight cell) -> remove authored row+dir -> forget graph run. Retiring the Python side first is what stops a running host call from writing after the authored branch disappears. Note the Python execution namespace is keyed by workspaceId (the child execution id), not threadId. Idempotent-ish: safe to retry after a lost response because authorization does not require an active row; the closed admission gate is never reopened. Callers treat it as fire-and-forget cleanup (supervisor guards with a `workspaceRemoved` flag and calls it on failure paths and on conflict).
sideEffects: Resolves the admitted principal; authorize_workspace_removal accepts already-retired rows (ownership-based, so a lost-response retry still succeeds)

PythonWorkspaceService::retire_thread(workspaceId): closes the execution admission gate permanently, cancels and drains any in-flight cell, shuts down the kernel, and rm -rf's the Python workspace directory on disk
AuthoredDocuments::remove_workspace: retires the workspace row in SQLite (transactional) and deletes the authored workspace directory from disk
GraphRunStore::forget(workspaceId): drops the in-memory latest graph run for that execution id
No Tauri events emitted

prose.callerUsage: restoreAuthoredState(input) with `{ input }`; the command handler destructures the struct itself and passes the fields positionally to the service.
prose.notes: `operationId` is a caller-owned idempotency key — retry with the same value. `mode` is snake_case on the wire. `forkedThreadId` is set ONLY for state_and_conversation and is where the UI must navigate afterwards. `document` is always the current projection; `revisionId` may already be superseded — check appliedToCurrentProjection. Restore never deletes revisions, so the pre-restore state stays in history.
prose.returns: AuthoredRestoreResult { documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection, document, forkedThreadId: string|null }
sideEffects: writes a NEW forward revision (restore is roll-forward, never history rewrite)
for mode='state_and_conversation', creates a forked thread sharing the immutable transcript prefix (forkedFromThreadId/forkedAtMessageId on the new AgentThread); the original thread is left intact
enqueues sync closure

prose.notes: Flat camelCase args, and the same thread-addressed kernel as run_python_cell. Fire-and-forget at the call site: bound to abortSignal's `abort` event with { once: true }, invoked with `void ... .catch(() => {})`, and the listener is removed in the run's finally block — the return boolean is discarded. Crucially, cancelling does NOT abandon the run: the caller still awaits run_python_cell so the transcript records whatever the cell emitted before interruption. If the turn is already aborted before the cell starts, the frontend short-circuits and never invokes either command.
prose.returns: boolean — true if a cell was in flight and got interrupted, false if there was nothing to cancel
sideEffects: Resolves the admitted principal and verifies the thread row is visible to it
Cancels the in-flight cell's cancel token — the worker gets the interrupt ladder; the running run_python_cell call still returns a terminal result with status "interrupted"
No Tauri events emitted, nothing written

prose.notes: annotations semantics are load-bearing: `null`/omitted ⇒ fall back to persisted scores (sorted z_index asc); `[]` ⇒ authoritative empty document, clears the scene (this is how deleting the last clip clears output). Callers always send the full live list (mid-drag args ahead of the DB). z_index and blend_mode are Scene metadata and deliberately excluded from the plan signature. The rAF-coalesced live path (store:499) fires per frame, so the command must be cheap and idempotent.
sideEffects: render_engine.set_active_scene(Some(scene)) — replaces the live render scene; set_active_scene(None) when annotations are empty or the built scene is empty
clear_plan_cache() when the annotation list is empty
reads/writes the process-global PLAN_CACHE (per-annotation compiled plan keyed by id + signature over pattern_id, venue_id, implementation_id, graph_revision, start/end, args) — incremental recompile
checks COMPOSITING_GENERATION before and after building; a concurrent leave_track/cancel_compositing makes the pass a no-op
resolves fixtures root + StorageRoot from AppHandle

prose.notes: Always called from an effect cleanup while `learning` is true. Same missing-venueId drift as controller_start_learn at both controller-config.tsx sites; those failures are silent (.catch(() => {})).
sideEffects: disarms learn mode (clears the stored app_handle) so MIDI resumes normal mapping

prose.notes: Ordering matters: the write lease is taken first, then connect, then the DB update, then commit — a failed connect aborts without persisting. Caller passes `currentVenue?.id ?? ""`, so an empty-string venue id reaches the backend and fails at the access layer rather than being guarded in the UI.
sideEffects: opens the MIDI input connection and installs the message callback
persists venue.controller_port = port_name (VenueAccess<Write>, committed)
emits `controller_port_change` { ports: string[] } on connect
the installed callback later emits `midi_learn_captured` (learn mode) and `controller_state`, and can push `universe-state-update`

prose.notes: Disconnect is sticky — it deliberately forgets the preferred port, so reconnecting requires an explicit controller_connect. Same `?? ""` venue-id fallback as controller_connect.
sideEffects: closes the MIDI connection
clears venue.controller_port so auto-reconnect stops (VenueAccess<Write>, committed)

prose.notes: Snapshot-then-subscribe: the UI calls this once on mount to seed state, then keeps it live via the `controller_state` Tauri event which carries the identical payload. A port must emit that event on every manual-layer mutation or the UI goes stale. groupIntensities only includes groups with a non-default intensity — absent key means default, not zero. activeCueIds = latched, flashCueIds = held.
prose.returns: ControllerState { active: boolean, masterIntensity: number, activeCueIds: string[], flashCueIds: string[], heldModifiers: string[], groupIntensities: Record<string, number> } (camelCase)
sideEffects: none — snapshot read

prose.notes: Polled on a 2s interval from both the Perform page and the controller config dialog — a port must keep it cheap and idempotent. Unlike mixer_get_status the doc comment does not promise auto-reconnect, but the polling cadence implies the same contract; verify against ControllerManager::status before porting.
prose.returns: ControllerStatus { connected: boolean, portName: string | null, availablePorts: string[] } (camelCase via ts-rs/serde)
sideEffects: VenueAccess<Read> lease only; auto-reconnect/dead-connection detection lives in ControllerManager::status

prose.notes: Must run before the status poll starts for auto-reconnect to work. Called once per venue load alongside mixer_init_for_venue and midi_reload_mapping; errors swallowed. Takes VenueAccess<Read> but binds it `mut` even though nothing writes.
sideEffects: seeds ControllerManager's preferred port from venue.controller_port (Option<String>) so the status poll can auto-reconnect without user action

prose.notes: Goes through RenderEngine, not ControllerManager, despite the `controller_` prefix — the manual layer is render state. Caller toggles against ctrlState?.active (undefined → treated as false → sends true) and guards on a truthy currentVenueId.
sideEffects: enables/disables the manual (controller) render layer inside RenderEngine

prose.notes: One-shot arm — the capture disarms itself, so a UI needs to re-arm per binding. DRIFT: both controller-config.tsx call sites invoke it with NO argument object, but venue_id is a required String — those two learn flows reject at the IPC layer and surface as setError(String(e)). Only perform-page.tsx:1026 passes { venueId }.
sideEffects: arms learn mode: the next parseable MIDI event emits a `midi_learn_captured` event (MidiInput payload) and is swallowed instead of being mapped; learn auto-disarms after one capture

prose.notes: Names are normalized (lowercase, spaces/hyphens -> underscore, non-alnum stripped, collapsed) for uniqueness but the raw name is stored; the error message quotes the *normalized* form. Empty-normalized names skip the check entirely, so multiple such groups are allowed. Axes are LR/FB/AB in -1..+1. movementConfig can't be set at create — it goes through update_movement_config. Caller optimistically appends a synthetic FixtureGroupNode with fixtureType 'unknown' and empty fixtures.
prose.returns: FixtureGroup { id, uid, venueId, name: string|null, axisLr/axisFb/axisAb: number|null, movementConfig: MovementConfig|null, displayOrder: bigint, createdAt, updatedAt }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the venue
Pre-check: lists all groups and rejects with "A group with name 'x' already exists" if normalize_group_name collides (in-transaction, not a DB unique constraint)
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()

prose.notes: Idempotent on requestId: retrying the same request returns the same pattern. Owner uid resolved server-side from StateDb auth (get_current_user_id) — never passed by the caller, and Option, so an unauthenticated create is allowed with uid = null. Name is normalized to snake_case in the frontend (toSnakeCase) before sending, not in Rust. The dialog keeps the requestId in a ref keyed by a fingerprint of [name, description] so an edited retry gets a fresh key. Category is a separate follow-up set_pattern_category call — creation and categorization are not atomic.
sideEffects: creates the pattern's authored document (per-document Git repo) + SQLite projection
engine.push_notify.notify_one() — wakes the sync push loop

prose.notes: requestId is REQUIRED and must be reused verbatim on retry — that is the whole idempotency mechanism. score-picker-dialog goes further and gates on a fingerprint of [userId, trackId, venueId, name] so a double-click reuses one requestId. Fails with 'track does not exist' if the track isn't in auth_visible_tracks. The bulk import path (track-browser:337) swallows all errors with `.catch(() => {})`.
prose.returns: Score — { id; uid: string|null; trackId; venueId; name: string|null; createdAt; updatedAt }
sideEffects: inserts a `scores` row
creates the score's git-backed authored document with an initial revision containing an empty score DSL file (SCORE_PATH)
score id is deterministic from (principal, "score", requestId) — a replayed requestId returns the existing score after fingerprint verification instead of creating a second one

prose.notes: Single `payload` object arg (NOT flat args like create_score — the two creation commands disagree on calling convention). requestId is the idempotency key. The created clip's stable id is `createdClipId`; find it inside `clips` (smoke.ts does exactly that) — `clips` is the FULL post-edit clip list, not a delta. `appliedToCurrentProjection: false` means a replayed operation committed historically but a newer edit is now live. No frontend caller yet — the UI creates clips through replace_track_scores; only the headless smoke test exercises this path.
prose.returns: TrackEditResult — { revision: string; clips: TrackClip[]; idMap: Record<string,string>; createdClipId: string | null; added: number; updated: number; removed: number; appliedToCurrentProjection: boolean }
sideEffects: commits a new revision to the score's git-backed authored document (commit message 'Create track clip')
rewrites the track_scores SQLite projection for that score
takes VenueAccess::<Write> on the score

prose.notes: Unlike update/delete, this one does NOT go through VenueAccess — it takes the pool directly (no venue exists yet to lock). description is nullable: the TS store coerces empty string to null (`description || null`). Caller ignores the returned Venue's freshness and immediately re-invokes list_venues via refresh().
prose.returns: Venue { id, uid, name, description, shareCode, role, controllerPort, mixerPort, mixerMappingJson, createdAt, updatedAt } (serde camelCase)
sideEffects: inserts a local venue row (role='owner'), marked dirty for the sync pusher

prose.notes: Caller optimistically removes the group and clears selectedGroupId, reverting to the captured previousGroups on error; returns boolean success to the UI. Deleting a group referenced by a saved selection expression is not checked — dangling name references stay dangling.
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the group; require_changed -> 'Venue resource not found' if not exactly 1 row
Membership rows go away with the group (FK cascade); invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()

prose.notes: Archive, not hard delete — consistent with the project's no-cascade-deletes rule. Principal comes from StateDb auth server-side; ownership enforcement lives inside archive_pattern, not in the command. Store calls refresh() (list_patterns) afterwards rather than removing optimistically.
sideEffects: archives (soft-deletes) the authored pattern document
engine.push_notify.notify_one()

prose.notes: Ownership-gated: if the score's owner != current principal it errors with the deliberately opaque 'score does not exist'. Replay-safe — an already-archived score returns Ok via completed_score_archive_replay. Arg is `id`, not `scoreId` (inconsistent with every other score command). Caller must also reset the track-editor store if the deleted score is the open one; the backend emits no event for that.
sideEffects: archives the score's authored document (git head recorded as archived — history is preserved, not rewritten)
under VenueAccess maintenance mode, DELETEs the score's track_scores rows then the scores row from the local projection
notifies the sync engine push loop (engine.push_notify.notify_one())

prose.notes: One track per call — bulk delete in the UI is Promise.all over N invocations, so a mid-batch failure leaves a partial delete (and the single catch logs only the first rejection). Errors with "Track {id} not found" on an unknown id or when the owner check rejects. Principal comes from StateDb server-side. The frontend deletes optimistically from the store BEFORE invoking and never rolls back on failure — a failed delete leaves the UI lying until the following refresh()/refreshBrowser() pair repairs it. This is a real hard delete of the track row + files (unlike delete_pattern, which archives) — the no-cascade-deletes rule is about sync, not this.
sideEffects: recovers any previously interrupted deletions first (recover_track_deletions)
BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: prepares the deletion plan, stages the track's files (audio, art, artifacts) for deletion on disk, deletes the row, commits — with filesystem rollback on any DB failure
the sync_delete_tracks SQLite trigger enqueues the committed row deletion for push

prose.notes: Deletes ONE clip. scoreId/trackId are explicit precisely so a retry after a lost success response can still resolve (the clip is already gone). track-score-commands.ts retries once with the same operationId; the second call must return Ok with removed=0 or the same result, never a missing-clip error. `clips` in the response is the full remaining clip list — callers can rebuild timeline state from it without a follow-up list_track_scores.
sideEffects: commits a delete revision to the score's authored document
rewrites the track_scores projection
VenueAccess::<Write> on the score

prose.notes: Owner-side delete. No cloud call here (contrast leave_venue, which does hit Supabase directly). Caller clears selectedVenueId when the deleted id was selected — note the caller compares `String(get().selectedVenueId) === id`, a stringify guard that hints selectedVenueId was once numeric.
sideEffects: BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction + commit
local venue row removed / tombstoned; sync push propagates

prose.notes: Pure path construction: dirs::audio_dir() (or ~/Music fallback) + 'Engine Library'. Does NOT check existence — always Ok — so callers probe with engine_dj_open_library and fall back to a directory picker seeded with this path. to_string_lossy means non-UTF8 paths are silently mangled rather than erroring.

Joins Track to PlaylistEntity on listId, ordered by title — NOT by the DJ's manual playlist order (PlaylistEntity has ordering columns that are ignored). Non-recursive: child playlists' tracks are not included. The generic adapter carries playlist keys as strings and converts with Number(playlistKey); an unknown id returns [] rather than erroring.
sideEffects: opens/closes a read-only pool

prose.notes: Flat list ordered by title, NOT a tree — parentId (Playlist.parentListId) must be assembled client-side. trackCount comes from a separate GROUP BY over PlaylistEntity, defaulting to 0 for playlists with no entries. i64 ids serialize as JS numbers (ts-rs override) — fine in practice for Engine's autoincrement ids. Issued in a Promise.all with engine_dj_list_tracks, so it opens a second concurrent pool on the same file.

prose.returns: PatternSummary { id, uid?, name, description?, categoryName?, createdAt, updatedAt, isVerified, authorName?, forkedFromId? }

prose.notes: Loads the whole graph document and throws away everything but `args` — same work as get_pattern_graph_document plus venue scoping. Both call sites pass implementationId: null and rely on venueId to pick the implementation; perform-page caches on the composite key `${venueId}:${patternId}`, which is the correct invalidation key because the args returned genuinely depend on the venue. Errors are swallowed per-pattern in track-editor (falls back to []).

Existence-checks the pattern first (get_pattern_pool) so an unknown id errors before document resolution. Passes venue_id = None, so implementation resolution here is venue-agnostic — get_pattern_args does the same load WITH a venue and can therefore resolve a different implementation for the same pattern. `revision` is the mandatory optimistic-concurrency base for save_pattern_graph_document. Callers must re-check `implementationId` in the response against what they asked for: both graph-agent and pattern-editor throw if the resolved implementation differs. smoke.ts:509 invokes it with `{}` deliberately to assert the missing-required-argument error path.

This is a GETTER with heavy write side effects — the whole identity-activation path hangs off it, because Supabase's storage adapter calls it on client construction. The storage adapter IGNORES its own `_key` argument and always sends SUPABASE_SESSION_KEY ("supabase_session"); the constant is duplicated in both TS and Rust (drift risk). Non-session keys ('display_name') take a trivial path. Can block on the sync lock and on a token-refresh network call — never assume it's fast.
sideEffects: for key == SUPABASE_SESSION_KEY only: takes engine.sync_lock, reserves the single StateDb connection, runs recover_committed_signout, may bootstrap legacy state and REFRESH an expiring token (network), begins an authored identity-switch barrier, arms write admission, and bootstraps authored live projections — rolling back write admission (leaving signed writes CLOSED) on failure
for any other key: plain read

prose.notes: SNAKE_CASE over the wire — AppSettings has no serde(rename_all), unlike every other model in the app; the TS side reads settings.max_dimmer. Storage is a string k/v table; the command applies the typing and defaults: audio_output_enabled true, artnet_enabled false, artnet_interface "0.0.0.0", artnet_broadcast true, artnet_unicast_ip "", net/subnet 0, max_dimmer 100 clamped to ≤100. Unparseable values silently fall back to the default.
prose.returns: AppSettings — { audio_output_enabled: bool, artnet_enabled: bool, artnet_interface: string, artnet_broadcast: bool, artnet_unicast_ip: string, artnet_net: u8, artnet_subnet: u8, max_dimmer: u8 }
sideEffects: read-only

prose.notes: Whole-file STANDARD base64 — a 10 MB mp3 crosses IPC as ~13 MB of string. Only justified because the bytes are fed to an LLM FilePart. mimeType is inferred from the file extension only (mp3→audio/mpeg, wav, flac, m4a|aac→audio/mp4, ogg; anything else → application/octet-stream), never sniffed. Contrast with album art, which deliberately does NOT inline base64 (CLAUDE.md). A port must not reuse this for playback.
prose.returns: { data: string; mimeType: string } — TrackAudioBase64, camelCase
sideEffects: reads the whole audio file off disk into memory

prose.notes: Untyped payload: the backend stores two JSON blobs and only validates that they parse. camelCase rename means the wire key is `tagOrder`. Returns null when classification hasn't run; the hook maps null → null state. A port must keep the JSON passthrough — there is no Rust-side schema for the classification shape.
prose.returns: { classifications: unknown; tagOrder: unknown } | null — both fields are opaque serde_json::Value re-parsed from TEXT columns

prose.notes: Nullable: `null` when beat detection has not run for the track. Every caller treats null as a soft miss (catch → null, or `if (!beats) return null`). Times are absolute seconds from track start. Rust type is models::node_graph::BeatGrid, exported to src/bindings/schema.ts by ts-rs.
prose.returns: BeatGrid | null — { beats: number[]; downbeats: number[]; bpm: number; downbeatOffset: number; beatsPerBar: number } (camelCase, seconds)

prose.notes: Null when drum transcription hasn't run. Keys are not guaranteed present individually — the e2e caller guards with `onsets?.kick`. This is the only command in this group that goes straight to the db module instead of services::tracks (minor layering inconsistency).
prose.returns: Record<string, number[]> | null — keys are the n2n class names `kick`, `snare`, `hat`, `cymbal`; values are onset timestamps in seconds

prose.notes: Read-through cache, not a pure read: first call for a track can take seconds and writes to the DB. Samples are interleaved min/max pairs per bucket (previewSamples.length = 2*buckets); bands/colors are the two generations of the same idea (colors is legacy interleaved RGB bytes). fullSamples/bands/colors are NOT cloud-synced — regenerated locally, so they can be null on a freshly pulled device. durationSeconds prefers decoded_duration and falls back to the tracks.duration_seconds metadata; callers (use-track-editor-store) use it as the timeline duration. All TS callers .catch(() => null) — treat failure as 'no waveform', not fatal.
prose.returns: TrackWaveform { trackId, uid: string|null, previewSamples: number[], fullSamples: number[]|null, bands: BandEnvelopes|null, previewBands: BandEnvelopes|null, colors: number[]|null, previewColors: number[]|null, sampleRate: number, durationSeconds: number }
sideEffects: Takes an AnalysisTaskGroup lease/epoch guard (cancellable analysis work)
On cache miss: decodes the audio file and computes the waveform, then upserts blobs into the local waveforms table and commits (ensure_track_waveform)
Logs '[waveform] track {id} published in {ms}ms' to stderr
Fails if the authenticated principal changes or track_hash changes mid-computation

prose.notes: The fine half of the waveform pair: get_track_waveform is a fixed 30 000 buckets however long the track is, this is exactly the visible range at exactly the caller's pixel density, measured from the audio each time. No AnalysisTaskGroup lease and no DB write — it is a view of the audio, not a stored artifact. Total by construction: the range is clamped to the decoded audio (the returned startSeconds/endSeconds are the clamped range, not the requested one) and the bucket count to 1..=16384, so a request past either end is answered rather than refused. Only the GPUI editor calls it today; the web timeline can adopt it unchanged, and should above ~FULL_WAVEFORM_SIZE/duration pixels per second, which is where its stored envelope runs out of buckets.
prose.returns: WaveformWindow { trackId, startSeconds, endSeconds, min: number[], max: number[], rms: number[] } — the three series are the same length, and it is the requested bucket count clamped to 1..=16384
sideEffects: VisibleTrackAccess::<Read> on the track, to read file_path/track_hash

Decodes the audio through audio::cache (process-wide LRU over the on-disk .pcm cache) on a blocking thread if it is not already resident — the same (hash, device rate) key host_load_track uses, so a track loaded for playback is already there
Writes nothing

sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue

prose.notes: Argument is `id`, not `venueId` (inconsistent with every other command in this fragment, which uses venueId). All three route wrappers re-fetch on every mount rather than reusing store state — deliberate, because `role` can change between sessions. The three call sites are literally the same effect copy-pasted three times (dedupe candidate).

sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on VenueResource::Venue(id) — errors if the venue is not accessible to the current principal

Overlaps list_tracks_enriched's venueAnnotationCount — the same number by two code paths, one of them raw SQL embedded in the command file instead of database/local/tracks.rs. That is the smell: it exists purely as a cheap refresh of one column after a venue switch.

prose.notes: Times are absolute track seconds on the way in; the host stores start_time as segment_start_abs, so every later host_seek/host_snapshot time is RELATIVE to the segment start. Errors on an empty range or empty decode. Re-checks that the authenticated principal did not change between the read and the operate access — a port must keep that check. beatGrid is passed through to LoadedSegment but the field is `#[allow(dead_code)]` — currently write-only.

replaces the loaded segment in the global HostAudioState — clobbers whatever host_load_track/host_load_segment loaded before
takes VisibleTrackAccess Read then re-takes Operate and commits (audit/access trail)

sideEffects: decodes the full track into the shared audio cache
replaces the loaded segment in the global HostAudioState
loads the beat grid from the DB itself (unlike host_load_segment, which takes it as an arg)

prose.notes: Returns unit, so it can never reject for an audio reason (only for IPC failure). Pausing with nothing loaded is a no-op.
prose.returns: void (infallible — Rust fn returns `()`, not Result)
sideEffects: stops advancing the playhead; stream outputs silence

prose.notes: Synchronous (non-async) command returning Result. Errors if nothing is loaded. The track-editor caller always does `host_seek(playheadPosition)` immediately before `host_play` — play does not resume from the UI playhead by itself.
sideEffects: starts the CPAL output stream / unmutes the persistent stream for the loaded segment

prose.notes: `seconds` is segment-relative, NOT absolute track time — matters for pattern-editor segments loaded with a non-zero startTime. The store's `scrub` variant optimistically sets currentTime + snapshotAtMs before firing a floating (unawaited) invoke, and handleSnapshot ignores incoming snapshot times while isScrubbing, to stop pre-seek snapshots yanking the playhead backward. Any port must preserve that ordering rule.
sideEffects: moves the shared fixed-point frame index consumed by the audio thread

prose.notes: Loops the whole loaded segment when no explicit loop region is set. host_set_loop_region ALSO sets this flag, so the two commands can fight: calling host_set_loop(true) with no region loops the segment, then a later clear via host_set_loop_region(null,null) silently disables looping. Two ways to control one flag — flag as a design smell.
sideEffects: flips the atomic loop flag read by the audio thread

prose.notes: The implicit `set_loop(start.is_some() && end.is_some())` is the load-bearing behaviour: clearLoopRegion passes both nulls to turn looping off. A half-specified region (one null) also disables looping rather than erroring. Store updates its local loopRegion optimistically before awaiting.
sideEffects: sets the loop region
implicitly enables looping when BOTH bounds are Some, disables it otherwise

prose.notes: The backend does NOT clamp — the caller clamps to [PLAYBACK_RATE_MIN, PLAYBACK_RATE_MAX] before invoking, and sets the store optimistically. A port that drops the frontend clamp will let a 0 or negative rate reach the audio thread. Rate changes pitch (no time-stretch).
sideEffects: updates the fixed-point playback-rate atomic read by the audio thread (resampling ratio)

prose.notes: This is a one-shot priming read only. The steady-state channel is the `host-audio://state` Tauri event, broadcast at ~15 fps (66 ms) by HostAudioState::spawn_broadcaster with the identical payload type. Both callers `listen()` first, then invoke host_snapshot once to fill the gap before the first broadcast. currentTime is segment-relative; the frontend extrapolates between snapshots using performance.now() (getExtrapolatedHostTime). A port must ship both the event and the command.
prose.returns: HostAudioSnapshot — { isLoaded: boolean; isPlaying: boolean; currentTime: number; durationSeconds: number; loopEnabled: boolean }
sideEffects: calls refresh_progress(), which pulls the atomic frame index into the mutex-guarded state before reading

prose.notes: No args at all — state comes from the AppHandle. Must run before search_fixtures (which errors 'Fixtures not initialized. Call initialize_fixtures first.'). Store ignores the returned count and immediately fires search('', true) then fetchPatchedFixtures(). Errors are swallowed by the caller.
prose.returns: usize — number of fixture definitions indexed
sideEffects: Walks the resolved fixtures root on disk (resolve_fixtures_root: bundled resource dir, else dev path) and builds a FixtureIndex
Replaces the in-memory FixtureState (Mutex<Option<FixtureIndex>>) managed state

Fixtures/groups/tracks are NOT pulled here — the frontend must fire sync_full after joining (join-venue-dialog.tsx:48 does exactly that, fire-and-forget). Errors from the RPC are wrapped as 'Failed to join venue: …'.

remote RPC join_venue_by_code creates the cloud membership row
inserts a local venue row whose id IS the cloud UUID and whose uid is the OWNER's uid, not the joiner's

errors 'Cannot leave a venue you own' when venue.is_owner()
requires auth; DELETEs venue_members where venue_id=eq.X&user_id=eq.Y in Supabase (failure only eprintln'd)
removes the local membership row

Two of the three callers only want `name` and filter out nulls (group names are nullable, so the selection-expression vocabulary is a filtered subset); group-expression-editor also dedupes and sorts. Ordering comes from the DB (displayOrder) and is relied on implicitly by perform-page's flat group list.

prose.notes: Unscoped by user despite the uid column. Both call sites load into ad-hoc local component state (no shared store) and swallow errors to console — duplicated fetch logic worth hoisting into one store in a port.
prose.returns: PatternCategory[] { id, uid?, name, createdAt, updatedAt }

prose.notes: No venue or user scoping and no pagination — returns every local pattern; the store filters client-side (`mine` by uid, `verified` by isVerified). track-editor's loadPatterns fans out one get_pattern_args call per returned pattern (N+1 over IPC).

Every score for a track that the current admission may see, in any venue, filtered in one statement by auth_write_admission — it never returns a sealed row from another principal. The gpui track editor's score rail reads this; the pattern editor uses it to find any venue's instance of a track. Replaced the empty-venueId overload on list_scores_for_track.
prose.returns: ScoreSummary[] — same shape as list_scores_for_track; `ordinal` is ranked within each (track, venue), so it repeats across venues.

prose.notes: Scoped to one venue. `uid` is the owner user id — track-session-store uses `s.uid === userId` for ownership/read-only. `annotationCount` is a joined COUNT, used by generate-dsl-dialog to pick a non-empty exemplar score. `ordinal` is a read-time ROW_NUMBER() rank by createdAt within (track, venue) — a display handle, never an identity; `venueName` is joined in so a cross-venue picker needs no second lookup.

prose.notes: Reads the SQLite projection of the authored document, not the git document. `args` comes back as a decoded JSON object (the row stores args_json TEXT); `blendMode` is decoded from a bare string column into the BlendMode enum. prose.returns: TrackScore[] — { id; uid: string|null; scoreId; patternId; startTime: number; endTime: number; zIndex: number; blendMode: BlendMode; args: Record<string, unknown>; createdAt; updatedAt }

Almost every field except id/trackHash/filePath/timestamps is nullable. Both the pattern-editor and generate-dsl-dialog use it as the seed of an N+1 fan-out (per-track list_scores_for_track / annotation loads) — a real candidate for a purpose-built enriched query.
prose.returns: TrackSummary[] (id, uid?, trackHash, title?, artist?, album?, trackNumber?, discNumber?, durationSeconds?, filePath, storagePath?, albumArtPath?, albumArtMime?, albumArtStoragePath?, sourceType?, sourceId?, sourceFilename?, createdAt, updatedAt)

prose.notes: The `has*` booleans are version-aware EXISTS checks against current preprocessor versions (registry::current_artifact_versions); a missing registered preprocessor falls back to version 0, which matches ANY row — so `hasX` can read true for a stale artifact when the registry lacks that table. venueAnnotationCoverageSeconds is #[sqlx(skip)], computed in Rust with overlapping intervals merged, not selected from SQL. With venueId=null the venue* counts are zero. Album art is a path, not bytes (deliberate — see CLAUDE.md). Headless scripts pass `{}` (venueId undefined => None).
prose.returns: TrackBrowserRow[] { id, uid?, title?, artist?, album?, durationSeconds?, albumArtPath?, albumArtMime?, sourceType?, filePath, createdAt, bpm?, annotationCount, venueAnnotationCount, venueAnnotationCoverageSeconds, hasStorage, hasBeats, hasStems, hasRoots, hasDrumOnsets, hasBarClassifications, hasGenres }
sideEffects: with venueId: takes VenueAccess::<Read> on that venue (an auth gate the venueId=null path skips entirely)

prose.notes: No VenueAccess wrapper — scoping lives in the SQL instead: it CROSS JOINs auth_write_admission and returns rows only while admission is armed/accepting/not-maintenance, matching venue.uid against admission.active_uid (guest ⇒ uid IS NULL AND role != 'member'). Consequence a port must keep: while write admission is closed (mid identity switch / sign-out) this returns an EMPTY list, not an error. `role` is COMPUTED per query from active_uid, not read from the stored column. Takes no arguments; the headless scripts still pass `{}`. Result order is unspecified — nothing re-sorts.
sideEffects: read-only

prose.notes: Unlike midi_reload_mapping this one propagates compile errors to the caller. deckId is u8 — values > 255 are a deserialization error, not a clamp. Called immediately after render_composite_deck for the same deck/track/venue; ordering matters (composite first, then cue compile). Doc comment claims it is 'called automatically after render_composite_deck' but that chaining is done in TS, not in Rust — drifted comment.

compiles all venue cues into RenderEngine cue_buffers keyed by (deck_id, cue_id) — stem decode via StemCache, FFT via FftService, fixture defs from resolve_fixtures_root, audio from StorageRoot

prose.notes: mode is Option<TriggerMode>; controller-config sends mode: null for continuous setIntensity bindings (no trigger semantics), and Rust falls back to TriggerMode::default() = tapToggleHoldFlash{300}. Field-name drift a port must reproduce exactly: the enum payload keys inside MidiAction / TriggerMode are snake_case (cue_id, group_id, threshold_ms) while the surrounding struct fields are camelCase — this is because the serde rename_all is on the struct, and the enum variants only rename the tag/variant name, not their fields. exclusive is set to requiredModifiers.length > 0 by controller-config.
sideEffects: commits the write transaction

prose.notes: Payload is nested under a single `input` key, not flattened. Optional fields are omitted (undefined) rather than null by the caller — e.g. args is only sent when non-empty. executionMode is a tagged union built client-side: { type: 'loop', bars: n } | { type: 'trackTime' }. Caller then immediately creates a fireCue binding with the returned cue id, so create-cue + create-binding are effectively one logical operation with no transactional link (partial failure leaves an orphan cue).
prose.returns: Cue (fully materialized row incl. id, uid, createdAt, updatedAt)
sideEffects: commits the write transaction (IMMEDIATE tx)

prose.notes: Note the nesting collision: the command argument is `input` and the struct field is also `input` (the MidiInput trigger) — payload reads { input: { venueId, name, input: trigger, groups } }. Caller sends groups: null explicitly when no groups are selected (never []). No mapping reload is triggered — controller-config's onCreated handler is what leads to midi_reload_mapping.
sideEffects: commits the write transaction

prose.notes: require_changed() — errors on missing id. Caller does not catch, so a failed delete rejects into the React handler unhandled.
sideEffects: commits the write transaction

prose.notes: Uses require_changed(): rows_affected != 1 errors with 'Venue resource not found', so deleting a non-existent id is an error, not a no-op — a port must not treat delete as idempotent. Buffer eviction happens after commit and is not rolled back on failure. Bindings referencing the cue are not cleaned up here.
sideEffects: commits the write transaction
drops compiled cue buffers for this cue from the RenderEngine (all decks)

Fires latch (not flash); pair with midi_release_cue. The UI derives on/off from ctrlState.activeCueIds, which comes from the emitted event, so the event is load-bearing, not just telemetry.

emits Tauri event 'controller_state' with a ControllerState snapshot
eprintln! diagnostics

Group map keys are fixture_id when head_index < 0, otherwise a per-head composite key. All three TS call sites .catch(() => {}) it. Heavy stderr logging including a dump of cue_buffers keys — production smell.

replaces the RenderEngine group→fixture map

Omitted fields are left untouched; there is no way to clear args/target back to NULL (Option<T>, not Option<Option<T>> like UpdateBindingInput.targetOverride / UpdateModifierInput.groups). prose.notes: Called from the learn-listener effect cleanup and from the dialog Cancel button; both fire-and-forget. Note it disarms learn but does NOT close a port opened by mixer_open_port — the temporary connection stays live until mixer_connect or mixer_disconnect.
sideEffects: disarms learn mode so CC traffic resumes mapping to faders

prose.notes: Mapping is serialised to JSON BEFORE the write lease is taken, so a bad mapping fails before touching the DB; connect precedes the DB write, commit last. channelFaders keys are 1-based deck ids (the UI builds 1..4 from fader_1..fader_4 and omits unmapped ones). After a successful connect the UI fabricates an initial MixerState with every mapped fader at 1.0 and crossfader 0.5 — the backend does not emit an initial state.
sideEffects: opens the MIDI input and installs the fader callback
persists venue.mixer_port + venue.mixer_mapping_json (mapping re-serialised to JSON by the command, VenueAccess<Write>, committed)
the callback emits `mixer_state` { channelFaders, crossfader } on every fader move, and `mixer_learned` { channel, cc } while learn is armed

prose.notes: Destructive: the saved MAPPING is dropped too, not just the port — the user must re-learn after disconnecting. Caller then locally sets mixerState null and patches mixerStatus { connected: false, portName: null } rather than re-polling.
sideEffects: closes the MIDI connection
clears both venue.mixer_port and venue.mixer_mapping_json so auto-reconnect stops (VenueAccess<Write>, committed)

prose.notes: Documented contract: call every ~2s; the poll IS the reconnect driver. A port must not treat it as a pure read or debounce it away. Caller declares the return shape inline as an anonymous type instead of importing MixerStatus from src/bindings/mixer.ts — drifted duplicate of a generated type.
prose.returns: MixerStatus { connected: boolean, portName: string | null, availablePorts: string[] } (camelCase; serialize-only, no Deserialize)
sideEffects: MixerManager::status performs dead-connection detection and auto-reconnect using the preferred config seeded by mixer_init_for_venue — this getter is NOT side-effect free

prose.notes: Must run before the 2s status poll or auto-reconnect never fires. Corrupt/unparseable mixer_mapping_json is swallowed to None via `.ok()` — the mixer then silently reconnects with no mapping instead of erroring; empty-string json is treated as absent. Called once per venue load next to controller_init_for_venue.
sideEffects: parses venue.mixer_mapping_json and seeds MixerManager's preferred (port, mapping) so mixer_get_status can auto-reconnect

prose.notes: Synchronous, no venue argument, no authorization — the only mixer command without a venue lease. Polled every 1.5s while the mixer dialog is open so hot-plug is detected; the dialog auto-selects ports[0] when nothing is chosen yet.
sideEffects: none

prose.notes: Learn-flow only: lets CC traffic reach the manager before the user saves a mapping. It replaces any live connection's mapping with the default (empty channelFaders, crossfader: None), so opening a port for learn silently disarms a working mixer mapping until mixer_connect is called again — flag this when porting. VenueAccess<Read> despite mutating manager state.
sideEffects: opens the MIDI port with an EMPTY mapping and does NOT persist anything to the venue DB

prose.notes: Requires an open port — the UI calls mixer_open_port first when nothing is connected. One-shot, so the dialog re-arms per learn target. On capture the UI clears any other target already bound to the same channel+CC, enforcing uniqueness client-side only; the backend does not.
sideEffects: arms learn: the next CC message emits `mixer_learned` { channel: u8, cc: u8 } (raw serde_json, not a ts-rs type) and is swallowed instead of being mapped to a fader; auto-disarms after one capture

prose.notes: No address-overlap validation server-side — the frontend computes the next free address (findNextAvailableAddress) and the auto label `${model} (${n+1})`. Spatial pose is not settable here at all: placement is a `venue_edges` row, not a fixture column. universe/address/numChannels are i64 on the wire but bigint in the TS type, so callers must pass plain numbers in and Number()-convert on the way back out (see :688 `universe: Number(fixture.universe)`). One call site ignores the return and refetches; two use the returned fixture's id.
prose.returns: PatchedFixture { id, uid: string|null, venueId, universe: bigint, address: bigint, numChannels: bigint, manufacturer, model, modeName, fixturePath, label: string|null, posX..posZ, rotX..rotZ }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Venue(venue_id); inserts a row and commits
Re-reads the full patch and pushes it to ArtNetManager (fixture_service::update_artnet_patch) — live DMX output changes
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()

prose.notes: StageLinQ path only — the Pioneer branch of the same store function calls the sibling perform_match_track_by_metadata (title/artist/bpm/durationSecs/venueId) instead. Never errors on 'not found': returns trackId=null with filename='' when the network path can't be parsed, and trackId=null with the parsed filename when no track matches. Takes tracks.first() with no tie-break, so duplicate filenames silently resolve to an arbitrary row. Track lookup is by source filename and is NOT venue-scoped, but the scores lookup IS — a track can match while hasAnnotations is false purely because the score lives in another venue. Caller guards a race by re-checking that the deck still holds the same track_network_path before applying the result.
prose.returns: PerformTrackMatch { trackId: string|null, hasAnnotations: bool, filename: string } (camelCase)
sideEffects: opens a read transaction on the venue; no writes

prose.notes: Pro DJ Link path only (StageLinQ uses perform_match_track). Match cascade is ordered: duration ±5s window (queried against the raw pool, NOT through the venue access lease) → BPM filter (exact/×2/÷2, 5% tolerance; passes through when either side has bpm<=0) → bigram Jaccard similarity of normalized 'title artist', min score 0.25, sorted desc, best wins. Empty title AND artist short-circuits to a null match. `filename` falls back to the basename of file_path (split on '/', so Windows paths would not split) when source_filename is null; on a miss it is "" not null. trackId is the only nullability signal.
prose.returns: PerformTrackMatch { trackId: string | null, hasAnnotations: boolean, filename: string } (serde camelCase)
sideEffects: none — read-only; takes a VenueAccess<Read> lease on VenueResource::Venue(venue_id)

prose.notes: Single-annotation version of generate_annotation_previews, driven live during a drag. LivePreviewInput has NO zIndex/blendMode (unlike compositor::LiveAnnotation) — the preview is always rendered alone with blend Replace, z 0, so it is per-clip output, not composite output. Host fills unset args from the pattern's arg defaults; the caller only sends overrides. Returned annotationId echoes the input id. Store coalesces: one in-flight call per annotation id, latest pending call replayed on completion.
sideEffects: read-only; compile + eval of one pattern over the preview column grid

prose.notes: Same as preview_pattern_image but for an UNSAVED graph — this is the graph-editor agent's 'look at my edit' tool. Same end_time > start_time guard and same Selection-forced-to-all default args, so the pattern-editor call site pre-rewrites graph.args via overrideSelectionArgs(...) to inject the editor's preview selection before sending. Requires a selected track context (venueId falls back to the current venue id, else empty string — an empty venueId will fail VenueAccess).
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue

prose.notes: Clamps: fps into [10, 30]; frame_count = ceil(duration*fps) clamped into [1, 256] — so a long span silently under-samples. Errors on duration <= 0 and on an empty pattern graph ("Pattern produced no output"). Args come from the pattern's own defaults with every Selection arg forced to "all" (merge_arg_values(graph, None, true)) — the hover card has no venue selection context, so preview colors/coverage will differ from a real run. Caller derives [startTime, endTime] from the enclosing downbeat bar and returns { frames, durationSec } with a cancel token; durationSec is recomputed frontend-side, the backend does not return it.
prose.returns: UniverseState[] — one frame per sample time
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> at entry, VenueAccess::<Operate> + commit at exit; errors if the principal changed mid-render
does NOT touch the render engine / live scene

prose.notes: Errors with 'end_time must be greater than start_time' if the span is non-positive — validate before calling. Args are the PATTERN DEFAULTS with every Selection-typed arg forced to `{"expression":"all"}` (preview_arg_values), so this is not what the timeline clip would render. Without beatGrid the column count falls back to the non-beat-aligned width rule. The `_at` variant takes (pool, StorageRoot, resource_root) directly — the AppHandle only ever supplied those two roots, so a port needs no Tauri handle.
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue

prose.notes: seed defaults to 12345 when absent — deterministic randomness for `random()` selectors, so a port MUST keep the same default or previews drift from evaluation. query is `.trim()`ed host-side. Store swallows errors and returns [] — invalid selection syntax is indistinguishable from an empty match at the call site (smell).
prose.returns: PatchedFixture[] (the resolver's ResolvedFixture list mapped to .fixture, order = resolver order)
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue

prose.notes: Pioneer CDJs (not Denon). deviceNum is the virtual player number this app claims — must not collide with a real deck; the UI defaults to 7 and the store falls back to 7 (`deviceNum ?? 7`). Same event-listener-before-invoke ordering requirement as stagelinq_connect; the two connects share one code path in the store selected by `source`.
sideEffects: claims the given device number on the Pro DJ Link network and starts the client
streams DeckEvent to the webview as `perform_event`

sideEffects: stops the client, releases the claimed device number, `perform_event` emission ceases
no-op when nothing is running

prose.notes: Returns Vec (never errors) — an empty list means 'nothing heard', not failure; if the socket can't bind, discover_cdjs also returns []. So a port cannot distinguish 'no CDJs' from 'networking broken'. The 3000ms timeout is not a parameter. TS mirrors the shape locally as `interface DiscoveredCDJ` in perform-page.tsx rather than using a generated binding — a hand-copied type that will drift.
prose.returns: DiscoveredDevice[] { player: u8, name, ip } — snake/flat, no rename_all; unique, sorted by player number
sideEffects: binds UDP port 50000 and passively listens for CDJ keepalives for a HARDCODED 3 seconds — the command blocks that long
no device-number claim, so it is safe to call while not connected

(already /100 from the int*100 column), durationSeconds? Every rekordbox_* read command reopens the DB fresh (with_db in subprocess.rs); there is no cached handle, so a port must expect per-call open cost. Errors are stringified (`Failed to open Rekordbox DB: ...`) or `Task join error: ...` on panic.

no writes, no events

The store does an optimistic local removal, and refetches the whole hierarchy after a per-head removal (because the split changes structure) and on any error. Group-scoped auth: the group id, not the venue id, is the resource.

invalidate_venue_fixture_cache() (process-global fixture cache)

Re-pushes patch to ArtNet; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()

prose.notes: Editor-side counterpart to render_clear_perform: only the active (track/pattern editor) scene, not deck layers. Universe designer pairs it with clearing the frontend universe + dmx stores so fixtures read as off.
sideEffects: sets RenderEngine.active_scene = None so the render loop emits nothing for the editor layer; takes VenueAccess<Read>

sideEffects: clears perform_layers, perform_deck_states and all cue_buffers; leaves manual_layer state intact; takes VenueAccess<Read>

prose.notes: Two-step by design: compositing targets active_scene and is then promoted, so it transiently clobbers whatever the editor had in active_scene. Venue authorization happens inside composite_track (this fn takes no explicit VenueAccess). Callers pair it with midi_compile_cues_for_deck for the same deck+track. Reserved deck id 99 is the simulated deck (render_engine.rs SIM_DECK_ID).

promote_active_scene_to_deck moves it (take) into perform_layers[deck_id] — active_scene ends up None
reads stems via StemCache and FFT via FftService (may compute/cache analysis)

prose.notes: Used when a CDJ deck has no matching Luma track: builds a synthetic beat grid from live BPM + beat-in-bar so beat-reactive cues stay in phase. beat_number is 1-indexed (1–4 in 4/4); position_secs is playback position at load time. resolve_fixtures_root failure is swallowed to None (.ok()) — silent degradation smell. Caller only invokes when bpm > 0 and deck.song_loaded.

reads fixture definitions from the resolved resources root and app storage root
takes VenueAccess<Read> on VenueResource::Venue(venue_id)

prose.notes: The only command in this fragment with NO venueId argument — the venue is derived from the fixture ids and every target must resolve to the same venue, otherwise it fails as one opaque not-found. Target grammar is `"fixtureId"` (whole fixture) or `"fixtureId:headIndex"`. Empty targets vector is an error at the authorize layer ("Identify requires at least one fixture target") but a no-op inside identify_targets — two contradictory guards. Callers fire-and-forget.

prose.notes: Hot path — called on every StateChanged frame and on every mixer state change; drives crossfade blending across decks. PerformDeckInput field names are snake_case on the wire (`deck_id`), unlike every other perform payload which is camelCase — the struct has no serde rename_all. Whole-vector replace means a deck omitted from `states` immediately drops to no state. Caller filters decks with sample_rate <= 0 and computes volume = channelFader * crossfaderWeight; time = samples / sample_rate. Errors are swallowed (.catch(() => {})).
sideEffects: replaces (does not merge) RenderEngine.perform_deck_states; takes VenueAccess<Read>

prose.notes: The ONE frontend primitive for multi-clip gestures — a whole-document compare-and-swap (base snapshot vs candidate snapshot), never per-row mutations. Caller builds operationId with crypto.randomUUID() and retries the *identical* request exactly once on failure (response-loss safety depends on operationId being reused verbatim). Response may return a main tip newer than the submitted candidate, so callers must rehydrate from result.clips and remap draft ids through result.idMap (rebaseTrackScoreIds/hydrateTrackReplacement in the same file). base/candidate arrays are normalized by trackScoreSnapshot before send. TrackScore.args is free-form JSON; ids in the candidate may be client-side drafts.
prose.returns: TrackEditResult { revision: string, clips: TrackClip[], idMap: Record<string,string|undefined>, createdClipId: string|null, added: number, updated: number, removed: number, appliedToCurrentProjection: boolean }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Score(score_id); rejects if score.uid != current principal, and if score.track_id != track_id
Commits a new revision to the score's per-document Git repo (authored state) under subject 'Replace track score'
Updates the SQLite projection of track_scores for that score
Idempotent on operation_id + request fingerprint (replay-safe); does NOT notify the sync engine (delete_score does — see issues)

prose.notes: Identical to get_track_waveform minus the cache lookup — both funnel into ensure_track_waveform. Caller pushes the result straight into useTrackEditorStore ({ waveform, durationSeconds }) only if the track is still the active one; a port must keep that staleness check or the editor shows another track's waveform.

Same AnalysisTaskGroup lease + principal/hash guards as get_track_waveform

Authorization is pinned to the durable parent thread (agentThreadId); agentExecutionId only namespaces Python workspace/run storage and defaults to thread_id. Venue fallback in the UI: `selectedInstance.venueId ?? currentVenue?.id ?? ""` — an empty venueId resolves selection to zero fixtures (black output), it is not an error. src/features/patterns/agent/graph-subagent-tools.test.ts:72 is NOT an IPC call site — it asserts an agent tool named `run_graph` exists.

prose.notes: Args are FLAT camelCase (not wrapped in `input`) — unlike the authored_state_* commands. The command always addresses the thread's own kernel: a subagent's cell is issued by run_python_cell_inner from inside the Rust turn loop, never over IPC, so there is no execution or workspace id on the wire. `scope` must be fully explicit: the tool fills every unknown field with null (see the test at python-tool.test.ts:225) — a port that omits keys instead of nulling them changes the wire shape. Scope fields are asserted against the thread's pinned subject and rejected on mismatch; the thread, not the caller, is the authorization principal. turnMessageId must name a durable `user` message already persisted in the thread before the model call; editable cells hard-fail without it. Figure budget: 8 MB total PNG per cell, over-budget figures are dropped with a human-readable notice in `notices` rather than truncated; the frontend then drops any single figure over MAX_PERSISTED_FIGURE_BYTES when storing, keeping width/height. `status: "error"` = Python exception (kernel healthy), `"failed"` = infrastructure failure (worker died/timeout), reason always in `notices`. The caller serializes cells per thread (enqueueCell) and converts any IPC throw into a synthetic `failed` result, so the tool never rejects.
prose.returns: PythonCellResult { status: "ok" | "error" | "interrupted" | "failed"; stdout: string; stderr: string; repr: string|null; traceback: string|null; figures: PythonCellFigure[] { artifactRel, width, height, base64Png }; notices: string[]; durationMs: number }

prose.notes: The returned `graph` is authoritative and may differ from what was sent (normalization) — the caller replaces its local state with a structuredClone of it, re-derives patternArgs from graph.args, and stores the new revision as the next baseRevision. `changed: false` means a no-op save (identical content). Two post-conditions are enforced in Rust and surface as plain error strings: the projection must be a PatternGraph (not a track projection) and its implementation_id must equal the requested one. The caller sends the whole invoke payload object straight through (`save: (input) => invoke("save_pattern_graph_document", input)`), so the TS input object's keys ARE the command's arg names — renaming one breaks silently at runtime. A fingerprint check skips the call when the graph is unchanged, and a generation gate (graphAuthorityGateRef) rejects the result if a newer load superseded it.

prose.notes: The single most side-effectful command in this fragment. Error strings are contractual: they distinguish 'previous session restored' from 'signed writes remain closed' and a port must preserve that distinction.
